titleZh: 酒店入住率下降，为什么电费没有跟着降？
titleEn: Hotel Occupancy Has Fallen. Why Has the Electricity Bill Not Followed?
summaryZh: 冬季入住率下降，电费为何不降？沿热源、输配、末端和热水系统开展能源体检，结合白天鹅与万豪公开案例、供热成本算例，选择维修、调校及改造措施。
summaryEn: Assess heat generation, distribution, room terminals and hot water to manage winter hotel energy costs, with public White Swan and Marriott cases, a worked heating-cost comparison and a prioritized action sheet.
contentZh:
酒店入住率下降，为什么电费没有跟着降？

进入采暖季，酒店入住率下降，电费却不一定跟着降：供暖需要补偿建筑向室外散失的热量，生活热水需要持续供应，设备效率和控制偏差也可能放大消耗。要控制冬季能源成本，应先沿着热源、输配、客房末端和热水系统做一次体检，找到热量损失和设备低效的位置，再决定维修、调校还是改造。

这不是给所有酒店设一个节能比例。北方集中供热、酒店自备锅炉、南方空调采暖，能控制的环节不同。但有一个共同问题值得先查清：酒店花钱买来的能源，有多少变成了需要的热量，又有多少消耗在没有解决的故障和不合理运行上？

冬季酒店电费，要放回供暖方式里看

先让工程负责人画出本店的供热关系：采暖和生活热水分别由什么设备提供，使用电、燃气还是外购热力，是否共用热源，哪些区域能够独立计量和调节。财务据此核对账单，才能知道该追踪哪一种能源。

燃气锅炉换成电热泵后，电费可能上升，燃气费却下降。集中供热按面积结算的酒店，即使用热减少，当季费用也未必相应减少。不能只看一张电费单就判断节能成败，也不能只看能源费用占营收的比例：房价和收入下滑，同样会把比例推高。

冬季的体检，应同时留下能源输入和服务结果。至少要有同一期间的用电量、燃气或外购热量、室外气温、采暖面积、实际营业情况，以及代表性客房温度和热水供应记录。月账单能看趋势，定位到某台设备则需要分表、运行记录或专业检测。

沿着热量走一遍，比先买设备更有效

第一处是热源机房：设备是否在合适的工况下运行。锅炉应由专业人员检查燃烧、换热和运行效率；使用热泵的酒店，应记录供热量、输入电量、供回水温度及辅助加热投入情况。不能拿设备铭牌上的额定效率代替整个系统在冬季的实际表现。

检查时要把“设备老了”和“设备确实低效”分开。供热量没有可靠计量，就先补检测；不能凭电表上涨直接推算热泵效率，也不能看到辅助加热启动就认定故障。它可能承担必要保障，是否投入过多需要结合设备设计、室外条件和控制记录判断。

第二处是热量输送路径：机房供出了热，是否有效送到客房。检查热水管、阀门及换热设备的保温是否破损、受潮，是否存在渗漏；对远端客房长期偏冷的问题，应核查管路流量、阀门与末端状态，再判断是否需要水力平衡。不要因为少数房间不暖，就不断提高整个系统的供水温度。

同时检查建筑能否留住热量：外门闭合、门窗密封和可见渗风是否异常。先修已经确认的缺陷；涉及防火门、排烟和必要通风的部位，不得以封堵换节能。

第三处是客房和公区末端：测温、控制与实际效果是否一致。选择朝向、楼层和距离机房不同的代表性房间，比较温控器读数、独立测温结果与客人实际使用情况。发现阀门关不严、传感器偏差或末端换热不良，应先确认故障，再修复和复测。

四管制等能够同时供冷供热的系统，还应检查是否存在不必要的冷热对冲。ASHRAE控制设计资料强调协调供冷供热，同时也保留湿度控制等特殊需要。工程人员必须结合设计判断，不能把所有同时供冷供热都当成浪费。

第四处是生活热水：少住客以后，热损失是否仍然很大。核对实际热水用量、进水与供水温度、循环回水和补热运行记录，检查管网保温、漏水与循环平衡。冬季进水温度与夏季不同，同样的用水量也不能直接按同样的加热负荷比较。

节能措施应以修复问题为起点。ENERGY STAR商业建筑检查清单列出了保温修补、温控器校准、盘管清洁和系统平衡等措施。具体能省多少，要回到本店测量；生活热水的储存、循环和出水温度，则须满足适用的卫生、防烫及设备要求，不能为了省电随意降低。

白天鹅宾馆：先做诊断，再提高供热效率

国家发展改革委2020年公布的白天鹅宾馆案例，记录了系统能源诊断后的综合改造。其中，燃油蒸汽锅炉被高效燃气蒸汽锅炉替换，披露的系统制热效率由60%提高到90%；改造后的蒸汽锅炉系统全年平均热效率为92.3%。

这组对比说明，改善热源效率可以减少提供相同热量所需的能源输入。若仅作原理演示，假设要提供100单位有用热量，60%效率需要约166.7单位输入，90%效率需要约111.1单位，后者少约三分之一。这是理想化计算，不是对该酒店节能率的重新测定。

该项目还采用了热回收热水系统。对冬季酒店而言，借鉴前必须先确认：本店是否有与热水需求同时存在、能够回收的余热。南方酒店全年运行条件下的成绩，不能直接当成北方严寒季的效果或预算依据。

万豪案例：体检结果怎样变成分项投入

美国明尼阿波利斯Marriott City Center提供了另一种参照。项目实施机构CEE于2026年3月公布，酒店先接受整栋建筑评估，再于2023至2025年分期实施改进。

其披露的年度节电量分项为：照明升级21万千瓦时，电机改造1.7万千瓦时，变频驱动安装49.7万千瓦时，制冷系统改进1.9万千瓦时，合计74.3万千瓦时。评估还识别了控制优化、阀门及风阀问题等机会。

值得比较的是投入依据：同一项目里，变频相关措施披露的节电量大于照明升级。但这不能推出每家酒店都应先装变频器。它给管理者的启发是，按检测结果和分项效益排优先级，而不是按设备是否常见来采购。这些是项目机构披露的全年成果，并非冬季单季数据，也未公开足以让其他酒店复算全部效果的原始记录。

选热源时，比较的是每单位有效供热成本

发现热源低效以后，也不能简单认定“换成热泵一定更便宜”。除了本地价格，还要看冬季实际工况、系统配套和新增电力费用。可以先做一个统一口径的比较，再决定是否值得深化设计。

以下全部是假设，仅演示算法。假设需要向供暖侧提供1000千瓦时热量，天然气价格每立方米3.5元，每立方米按10千瓦时热值计，锅炉效率90%；电价每千瓦时0.8元。比较中暂不计锅炉辅机电耗和不同方案的额外输配损失。

燃气锅炉需要约111.1立方米天然气，燃料费约389元。若热泵系统同期供热量与总输入电量之比为3，需要约333.3千瓦时电，费用约267元；若这一比值降到2，则需500千瓦时电，费用400元。

同一组价格下，运行表现变化就可能让费用排序翻转。因此，供应商给出一个额定性能系数，还不足以决定采购。用于比较的热泵输入，应覆盖约定边界内主机、水泵和辅助加热等用电，并采用当地冬季工况；天然气热值和价格也应使用本店实际数据。

这还只是运行能源费用。正式投资比较须再计入设备、施工、维护、供电容量及相关收费、营业影响等差异。投入回收期应依据可解释的年度净节省测算，不能把一个寒冷日的结果乘以全年天数。

把冬季体检做成一张有优先级的措施表

总经理可让工程负责人牵头，将热源、输配、末端和热水系统各列一行，再按下面的字段逐项填写。没有的数据注明待测，不先给出节能承诺。

现状与证据：设备和位置、实测值、测量期间、正常依据、故障或低效判断。要写到“哪段保温破损”“哪个阀门关闭后仍持续供热”，不能只填“能耗偏高”。

拟采取的措施：维修、调校或改造，分别说明解决哪一种损失。已经证实的漏损和控制故障，优先评估修复；热源更换、变频及热回收等项目，再依据工况、可实施性和收益比较安排。

资源与责任：工程技术负责人、使用部门、预计停用范围、施工和复测费用。财务核对完整成本，总经理协调服务安排，超出授权的投资由业主决定。

验收与退出：测什么、与哪段基线比较、服务条件如何保证，以及哪些异常出现后应撤回调整或重新评估。施工完成不等于节能成立，费用下降也需要解释原因。

先选一项有证据、可实施、能够复测的措施做起。例如，一段已确认受潮破损的热水管保温，可以在工程确认材质、施工和防火要求后修复，记录修复范围，并在相近运行条件下复测相关损失与补热需求。若现有计量无法识别节省量，可以确认修复质量，却不应硬报节能百分比。

冬季能源控制，最后要同时过两道验收

一道是能源与费用。比较前后要对齐天气、采暖范围和热水服务，分别看电、燃气及外购热力；条件差异明显时，应由专业人员校正基线，再评价净节省。热源转换后，必须同时核查减少和增加的能源项目。

另一道是服务与设备。检查代表性客房温度、热水供应、设备报警和必要通风；发生供暖不足、热水异常或防冻风险，应按工程预案及时恢复并排查。没有客诉，不等于服务条件已经合格。

酒店冬季节能的第一步，是把热量从哪里来、损失在哪里、怎样改和改后如何验证写清楚。让一次体检形成有证据的措施优先表，业主才知道钱该投在哪里，工程团队也有依据守住能源成本和服务质量。

Hotel Occupancy Has Fallen. Why Has the Electricity Bill Not Followed?

During the heating season, a fall in hotel occupancy does not necessarily bring a corresponding fall in electricity bills. Space heating must replace heat lost from the building, hot water must remain available, and inefficient equipment or control faults can increase consumption. To manage winter energy costs, start with an assessment of heat generation, distribution, room terminals and domestic hot water. Locate heat losses and inefficient operation before deciding whether to repair, tune or replace equipment.

This does not mean setting one savings target for every hotel. District heating in northern China, an on-site boiler and air-conditioning-based heating in southern China offer different opportunities for control. They share a question, however: how much purchased energy becomes useful heat, and how much is consumed by unresolved faults or inappropriate operation?

Understand winter electricity costs in the context of the heating system

Have the engineering lead map the hotel's heating arrangements first: which equipment provides space heating and domestic hot water, whether it uses electricity, gas or purchased heat, whether the services share a heat source, and which areas can be metered and controlled separately. Finance can then identify the energy bills that need to be tracked.

Replacing a gas boiler with an electric heat pump may increase electricity costs while reducing gas costs. A hotel billed for district heating by floor area may not see its current-season charges fall when it uses less heat. One electricity bill cannot establish whether energy management has improved. Nor can energy costs as a share of revenue: falling room rates and revenue can raise that ratio too.

A winter assessment should record both energy inputs and service outcomes. At a minimum, align electricity consumption, gas or purchased heat, outdoor temperature, heated floor area, actual business activity, representative room temperatures and hot-water service records for the same period. Monthly bills show trends; locating a problem in a particular machine requires submeters, operating records or professional testing.

Follow the heat before buying equipment

The first check is the plant room: is equipment operating under suitable conditions? Qualified personnel should assess boiler combustion, heat transfer and operating efficiency. For a heat-pump system, record heat output, electricity input, supply and return water temperatures, and auxiliary-heating operation. Nameplate efficiency cannot stand in for the whole system's actual winter performance.

Distinguish old equipment from demonstrably inefficient equipment. Where heat output cannot be reliably measured, arrange additional testing. An increase at the electricity meter alone cannot establish heat-pump efficiency, and auxiliary heating starting up does not by itself establish a fault. It may provide necessary backup; whether it runs excessively depends on the design, outdoor conditions and control records.

The second check is the distribution path: does heat leaving the plant reach the rooms effectively? Inspect insulation on hot-water pipes, valves and heat-exchange equipment for damage or moisture, and check for leaks. Where distant rooms remain cold, investigate flow, valves and terminal condition before deciding whether hydronic balancing is required. Do not keep raising the entire system's supply temperature simply because a few rooms are cold.

Check whether the building retains heat as well: look for exterior doors that do not close properly, defective window and door seals, and evident draughts. Repair confirmed defects first. Do not seal fire doors, smoke-control provisions or necessary ventilation to save energy.

The third check is room and public-area terminals: do temperature readings, controls and actual conditions agree? Select representative rooms with different orientations, floors and distances from the plant. Compare thermostat readings, independent temperature measurements and actual guest use. Confirm suspected leaking valves, sensor errors or poor terminal heat transfer before repairing and retesting them.

In four-pipe and other systems capable of simultaneous heating and cooling, check for unnecessary conflict between the two. ASHRAE's controls guidance calls for coordination while recognizing exceptions such as humidity control. Engineers must assess the design rather than treating all simultaneous heating and cooling as waste.

The fourth check is domestic hot water: do substantial heat losses persist when fewer guests are staying? Review actual hot-water use, inlet and supply temperatures, circulation return conditions and reheating records. Inspect pipe insulation, leaks and circulation balance. Winter inlet-water temperatures differ from summer conditions, so the same water volume cannot automatically be treated as the same heating load.

Start energy measures by addressing identified problems. ENERGY STAR's commercial-building checklist includes insulation repairs, thermostat calibration, coil cleaning and system balancing. Savings still need to be measured at the hotel. Hot-water storage, circulation and delivery temperatures must satisfy applicable hygiene, scald-protection and equipment requirements; they should not be lowered indiscriminately to reduce electricity use.

White Swan Hotel: diagnose first, then improve heat-generation efficiency

A White Swan Hotel case published by China's National Development and Reform Commission in 2020 describes a comprehensive retrofit following an energy assessment. Replacing oil-fired steam boilers with efficient gas-fired boilers increased the reported heating-system efficiency from 60% to 90%. The retrofitted steam-boiler system's annual average thermal efficiency was reported as 92.3%.

The comparison illustrates how better heat-generation efficiency can reduce the energy input needed to deliver the same useful heat. As a simplified illustration, supplying 100 units of useful heat at 60% efficiency requires about 166.7 input units; at 90%, it requires about 111.1 units, roughly one-third less. This is an idealized calculation, not a new measurement of the hotel's savings rate.

The project also used a heat-recovery hot-water system. Before applying that approach in winter, establish whether the hotel has recoverable waste heat available at the same time as hot-water demand. Results from year-round operation at a southern Chinese hotel cannot directly establish performance or budgets for a severe northern winter.

The Marriott case: turn an assessment into specific investments

Marriott City Center in Minneapolis, United States, offers another reference. In March 2026, project delivery organization Center for Energy and Environment, or CEE, reported that a whole-building assessment had preceded phased improvements implemented from 2023 to 2025.

Reported annual electricity savings were 210,000 kWh from lighting upgrades, 17,000 kWh from motor retrofits, 497,000 kWh from variable-frequency drive installations and 19,000 kWh from refrigeration improvements, totaling 743,000 kWh. The assessment also identified opportunities involving controls, valves and dampers.

The basis for investment is the useful comparison. Within this project, reported electricity savings associated with variable-frequency drives exceeded those from lighting upgrades. That does not mean every hotel should install drives first. It illustrates why measured findings and the benefits of individual measures should determine priorities, rather than the familiarity of a product. These are annual outcomes reported by the project organization, not winter-only data; the published material does not include sufficient raw records for another hotel to reproduce the full assessment of results.

Compare heat sources by the cost of useful heat delivered

Finding an inefficient heat source does not establish that switching to a heat pump will be cheaper. Local prices, actual winter performance, supporting systems and additional electricity charges all matter. Begin with a consistent comparison before deciding whether detailed design is justified.

The following figures are entirely hypothetical and illustrate the calculation only. Assume 1,000 kWh of heat must be delivered to the heating side. Gas costs RMB 3.5 per cubic metre and has an assumed calorific value of 10 kWh per cubic metre; boiler efficiency is 90%. Electricity costs RMB 0.8 per kWh. The comparison temporarily excludes boiler auxiliary electricity and differences in additional distribution losses between the options.

The gas boiler requires approximately 111.1 cubic metres of gas, costing about RMB 389. If the heat-pump system's heat output divided by its total electricity input over the same period is 3, it needs about 333.3 kWh of electricity, costing approximately RMB 267. If that ratio falls to 2, it needs 500 kWh, costing RMB 400.

At the same energy prices, operating performance can therefore reverse the cost ranking. A supplier's rated coefficient of performance is insufficient to decide a purchase. Heat-pump input used in the comparison should include the main unit, pumps and auxiliary heating within the agreed measurement boundary, under local winter conditions. Use the hotel's actual gas calorific value and prices too.

These are operating energy costs alone. A formal investment comparison must also include differences in equipment, construction, maintenance, electrical capacity and related charges, and disruption to business. Calculate payback from supportable annual net savings; do not multiply one cold day's result by the number of days in a year.

Turn the winter assessment into a prioritized action sheet

The general manager can ask the engineering lead to create separate rows for heat generation, distribution, terminals and hot water, then complete the following fields. Mark unavailable data as requiring measurement rather than promising savings in advance.

Condition and evidence: equipment and location, measured values, measurement period, the basis for normal performance, and the finding of a fault or inefficiency. Identify the damaged insulation section or the valve that continues to pass heat when commanded closed, rather than writing only that consumption is high.

Proposed measure: repair, tuning or replacement, with the loss each addresses. Assess confirmed leaks and control faults for repair first. Rank heat-source replacement, variable-frequency drives and heat recovery according to operating conditions, feasibility and comparative benefits.

Resources and responsibility: engineering lead, operating department, expected shutdown scope, construction and retesting costs. Finance checks complete costs, the general manager coordinates service arrangements, and the owner decides investments beyond delegated authority.

Acceptance and withdrawal: what to measure, which baseline to use, how service conditions will be maintained, and which abnormalities trigger reversal or reassessment. Completion of construction does not establish energy savings, and a lower bill still requires an explanation.

Start with a measure that has evidence, is feasible and can be retested. For example, repair a section of confirmed wet and damaged hot-water pipe insulation after engineering has checked materials, construction and fire-safety requirements. Record the scope and retest relevant losses and reheating demand under comparable operating conditions. If available metering cannot identify savings, the repair quality can be confirmed, but a savings percentage should not be invented.

Winter energy control needs two forms of acceptance

The first concerns energy and costs. Align weather, heated areas and hot-water service when comparing periods, and track electricity, gas and purchased heat separately. Where conditions differ materially, qualified professionals should adjust the baseline before assessing net savings. Following a heat-source change, check both the energy inputs that decreased and those that increased.

The second concerns service and equipment. Check representative room temperatures, hot-water supply, equipment alarms and necessary ventilation. If heating becomes inadequate, hot-water conditions become abnormal or freeze-protection risks arise, restore operation and investigate promptly under the engineering plan. An absence of guest complaints does not establish that service conditions are satisfactory.

The first step in winter hotel energy management is to establish where heat comes from, where it is lost, what should change and how the result will be verified. An assessment that produces an evidence-based priority list helps owners decide where to invest and gives the engineering team a sound basis for protecting both energy costs and service quality.
